title: Author of Good, to Thee We Turn
description: Author of Good, to Thee We Turn in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: James Merrick wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 430 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Holy Resignation”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Au-thor of good, to thee we turn: Thine ev-er wake-ful eye A-lone can all our wants dis-cern, Thy hand a-lone sup-ply.

lines: Author of good, to thee we turn:
Alone can all our wants discern,
O, let thy love within us dwell,
That love shall vainer loves expel,
And, O, by error's force subdued,
We blindly shun the latent good,
Not what we wish, but what we want,
The good we ask not; Father, grant;

licence: Public domain: James Merrick died in 1769.
credits: Words by James Merrick (1720–1769), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
